analysis.title: Positioning For A Hawkish FOMC
key_insights: TS Lombard expects the Fed to lean very hawkish at the 28 October 2026 meeting, citing strong US macro data.

US 10y yields have risen about 30bp since peaking in early October. The report attributes the move to markets assigning a higher probability to an AI bust scenario, which could prompt aggressive Fed cuts.

If AI-bust angst fades, US rates would face renewed upside pressure because the macro backdrop looks hawkish: initial jobless claims at their lowest in 57 years, solid growth, and an upside inflation surprise this month.

Global price pressures are not abating. Oil prices have risen again with a term structure pointing to higher for longer, ISM prices paid and S&P Global PMI output prices remain high, shipping costs are elevated, and food price inflation is in the pipeline.
New York Fed survey inflation expectations keep rising, and Fed speak and the Fed minutes read as very hawkish.

Much of current US inflation comes from non-persistent factors (energy, tariffs, AI capex), but Kevin Warsh wants inflation back to target in a timely manner after almost six years of misses. The Fed is therefore less likely to wait for disinflation to appear.

Homebuilder fundamentals are poor: margins are below pre-Covid levels, new home prices are falling, input costs (labour, materials, financing, tariffs) are rising, construction starts are weakening, inventory is rising, and the NAHB prospective buyer component is at its lowest since the Covid-19 recession.
New trade: long S&P 500 equal weight (RSP) vs short homebuilders (XHB) at a 1.75:1 ratio to adjust for volatility differences.

Portfolio update: the long Taiwan vs short India equity trade hit its stop at +14% P&L. The long Japanese banks trades hit their stop at -5% and will not be re-entered. The portfolio stays long 2y Canadian vs short 2y Japanese government bonds.
TS Lombard still likes Tech but will wait for the Fed meeting before adding new Tech-focused trades.

tension_points.bull_case: If AI-bust angst dissipates, strong US macro (record-low claims, solid growth, upside inflation) would push US rates higher, which is hawkish for the Fed and negative for homebuilders.
tension_points.bear_case: The recent rise in yields reflects a higher probability of an AI bust, which could prompt the Fed to cut rates aggressively.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A materialization of the AI bust scenario that leads the Fed to cut aggressively.
